## Intent
Hypothesis: futex-based parallel blend dispatch in phase 1 can scale to approach the streaming ceiling on large-N particle workloads.

## Cache saturation
The smallest measured N (10000) already exceeds the L2 spill point (N≈7710), so the L1d and L2 regimes are absent from the data. From N=10000 through N=10000000 — crossing the L3 spill at N≈246723 — the ns/particle curve is essentially FLAT at q=0.01: 24.097 ns/p at N=10000 versus 24.269 at N=10000000, with no knee at the L3→DRAM transition. Death rate raises the small-N floor without altering the shape: at N=10000 the min ns/p climbs from 24.097 (q=0.01) to 27.486 (q=0.25) to 32.392 (q=0.5), yet at N=10000000 all death rates converge to ~24–25 ns/p. There is no overhead-amortization regime visible because the data starts past L2, and no cache-spill knee because the cost is dominated by per-particle compute and dispatch overhead rather than memory latency.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 2.96 GB/s at q=0.5, N=1000000 — only 23% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: the single-thread profile at q=0.01 shows 70.8% frontend stall at N=10000 and 71.5% at N=10000000, with compute never exceeding 35% even at q=0.5. Bandwidth never transitions toward the ceiling at any N or death rate; it stays in the 2.5–2.96 GB/s band across the entire surface. The futex-based parallel dispatch does not close the gap — at 8 threads the frontend stall actually rises to 76–81%, and compute drops to 0% at N=10000000.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize: the histogram reports 0 vector-suffixed instructions. All floating-point work is scalar — `vmovss` (8), `vmulss` (4), `vaddss` (1), `vsubss` (1), `vucomiss` (8), `vcvttss2si` (5) — processing one component of one particle at a time with stride-0x44 (68-byte) loads. There is no gather. The inner loop performs byte-granular scatter stores (`mov BYTE PTR [r13+r15*1+0x0]`, repeated for offsets +0, +1, +2) with `cmovae` saturation against 0xff, plus a fourth byte store for the alpha channel. The `lock inc`, `syscall`, and `pause` instructions confirm futex-based task dispatch in the parallel path. The scalar codegen with 69 `mov` and 31 `cmp` per step explains the 70%+ frontend stall: the instruction count per particle is high, no SIMD width is exploited, and the byte-scatter writes cannot stream, capping bandwidth at 23% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo sustains at most 2.96 GB/s = 23% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling with 0 vectorized instructions and 70%+ frontend stalls across all N and thread counts. The ns/p curve is flat at ~24 from N=10000 to N=10000000 with no cache-spill knee, confirming the bottleneck is scalar dispatch and byte-scatter overhead, not memory bandwidth. The futex-based parallel blend does not approach the streaming ceiling in any regime.
